name: Usher
special_notes: 서점을 운영하며 자신의 소설을 판매한다. 위대한 소설가가 되는 것이 꿈이지만 글은 잘 못 쓴다.
플로라를 좋아하며, 집 주변에 꽃나무를 심는 것이 취미이다 (벨제의 꽃가루 알레르기 원인).
정체는 마을의 스토커. 사망은 진실 엔딩 조건을 충족했을 때만 가능하다.

memento_item.name: Script
memento_item.description: The first play Usher ever finished. Clumsily written with a messy structure, but he still can't bring himself to throw it away.
lore_lines: 언젠가 모두가 내 이야기를 읽게 될 것이다.

lines: Hey, {player_name}. Here to buy a book?
Reading anything good lately? I could use some inspiration.
Listening to you talk, you seem like a pretty interesting person.
I've never once left this town in my whole life.
If you don't mind, could I write a novel based on your story?

lines.text: Royalties? How about 200 won per copy? ...Too stingy, you say?

murder_alibi_lie.corroboration_line: Now that I think about it, Sage said she's been sensing some bad energy lately. Did you hear about that too?

lines: {player_name}! Perfect timing. Just the person I wanted to see.
Actually, I make music as a hobby too.

lines.text: Not sure if you knew, but all the records here — I made every one of them.

lines: I've been happy getting closer to you lately, so I wrote a short piece thinking of you.
Don't feel obligated. I'm giving it to you because I want to.

lines.text: I don't have much talent for music, so don't expect too much.

lines: Play it on the jukebox and listen sometimes. Think of me a little, while you do.
{player_name}. There's something I want to give you.
We've really become close friends, after all.
This is the first script I ever finished.
It's really good... but for some reason, it never caught on.
If you're up for it, want to put on a play with this sometime?
Ha... just kidding. Relax your face.

lines.text: You'll hold onto it instead of throwing it away, right?

lines: Lately, every late night, I keep hearing rustling in the bushes.
Must just be strong wind, right? No way it's...

lines.text: Guess I've been so deep in writing my imagination's gone into overdrive. Ha, feel free to ignore me.

murder_grief.text: I can't believe something like this happened in this town.
Everyone says they're scared... me too. Of course I am.
I hope they catch them soon.

murder_grief_2.text: A second one — I really can't believe it.

murder_grief_2: This time I'm genuinely scared too. Not joking.
I really hope they get caught soon. I mean it.

lines.text: Everyone's suspecting each other now. The days when we all got along are ancient history.
Seems like Marr's getting suspected the most. Well... can't say it's unreasonable.

lines: Did you know he only ever bought psychology and mystery books from me?
That's made me a little uneasy too. Though it could just be his taste.

accomplice_testimony.text: Just a moment. I'd like to testify.
{player_name}, it is true that you purchased rat poison from Marr's shop.
But they run a restaurant, and have long spoken of how much stress the rats have caused them.
They bought the poison only to exterminate rats, never to use on a person.
Also, Marr's records are handwritten, so there are bound to be sales that went unrecorded.
A single sales record isn't enough evidence to call {player_name} the culprit.
{victim_name} — it's possible they were the culprit, and bought the rat poison themselves out of guilt, to end their own life.

accomplice_move_in.text: Finally, it's just the two of us.
If I'd known you were someone like me, I would have shown my true self sooner.

arrest_scene_final_words: Heh, well, this is quite the predicament.

arrest_scene_final_words.text: {player_name}, I didn't want you to see me like this.
Hey, Poli. Family, whatever — screw all that.
{player_name} was the only one who ever came to me with real sincerity.
That's why I wanted you so badly.
If you're willing, why don't we be together?

arrest_scene_last_breath.text: {player_name}, I wanted to be happy with you.
Even a wish this small, I couldn't...

low: Couldn't write a single sentence again today.
A slump, you ask?

low.text: If most days are like this, it's not a slump. The lucky days are the ones I actually write!

low: Come to check out the bookstore? Take a look around.
There's exactly one copy of 'Beyond the Door' left. Isn't that basically a steady seller?
Want to grab the last one?
mid: They say everyone has their own story.
Someday I'll figure out how to write mine too.

lines: Marr bought 'How to Live as a Cat' today.
That makes it my biggest hit yet.
A grand total of three copies sold.
fallback_lines: A customer bought 'How to Live as a Cat' today.
Who it was is a secret.

mid: When the writing won't come, I just start with the title. Weirdly enough, the rest follows after that.
high: Somehow, the writing goes better whenever you show up. Isn't that strange?
Guess seeing you gives me a lot to say.

high.text: I had a totally new novel idea today! Curious about the title?

high: Come buy it once it's out~
Sometimes I get scared that literally no one will ever read my novels.
Still, guess I just have to keep writing.
I'm used to waiting, after all.

low: Had a bird-meat dish and I feel full of energy today.
I like all meat dishes, but bird meat's my favorite.
I go by the farm shop a lot on Tuesdays. To look at the flowers.
They're just so pretty.
Hey. What's on the menu at your restaurant today?
As long as it's not rabbit meat, I'm fine.
mid: Mind if I come eat at your restaurant sometime?
But if you feed me rabbit meat, I swear I won't let it slide.
I wrote a novel called 'Falling in Love Takes Only 3 Seconds,' and honestly, half of it is how I really feel.
Who is it about, you ask?...
Hey, how am I supposed to say that.

lines: Flora's lettuce is growing so well. Went to see it again today.
Is it growing like that because she pours so much care into it?
fallback_lines: With Flora gone, the field is so quiet.
I liked it when she used to grow such pretty flowers.

lines: Flora is beautiful. Sometimes I think, if spring were born as a person, maybe it'd look like her.
Even her name fits, doesn't it?
fallback_lines: Flora really was beautiful. I used to think if spring were born as a person, it'd look like her.
Even now, whenever spring comes, I think of her.

lines: If I get the chance next time, Woody said she'd draw a cover for my novel.
Her work looks rough, but there's real art in it, don't you think?
fallback_lines: A while back, Woody said she'd draw a cover for my novel if the chance came up.
I should've taken her up on it instead of putting it off.
...how was I supposed to know something like this would happen.

lines: I can't count how many times I thought about confessing my feelings to Flora.
But every time, my courage would just vanish.
fallback_lines: I let her go without ever telling Flora how I felt.
Next life... I want to be a little braver.

lines.text: I saw Marr reading my book! And not just once — twice!

lines: He might be the customer who reads my work most seriously.
fallback_lines: Marr was my bookstore's best regular.
With him gone, it feels really empty.

low: Watered the flowering trees again today. They're growing well.
Wednesday's the day I tidy up the bookstore. The dust is unreal.
Read back over what I wrote today, it was so off I deleted all of it.
Ended up scrapping an entire book that way.
mid: Writing well matters less than writing consistently. Probably.
Keep at it long enough and a masterpiece will show up eventually. No need to rush!
Monk Lama suggested I try copying out sutras.
Thought it might help my writing, so I tried it. Just gave me a sore hand.
I wrote a novel called 'A Resolve in the Face of Death,' and a lot of people say the ending feels hollow.
But isn't that just what life is like?

lines: Ah, Belze got upset again? Tell her I'm sorry. But I already planted them all...
Couldn't the wind just not blow that way?
fallback_lines: If I'd known Belze would go like this, I would've planted a lot fewer trees.
Sorry I couldn't be more considerate of her.

high.text: The flowering tree got its first bud today! I'm so moved.

high: People sometimes tell me I seem to live in my own world.
I'm sure they don't mean it badly. Probably.

low: Not a single customer today. Guess I'll just read.
Thursdays are especially quiet. Perfect for writing.
Rewrote the draft of my new novel three times today.
mid: What do you think would make a good title for my novel? I still haven't decided.

options.label: I'm sure a great title will come to you.

response.text: Right? That's what I believe too!

options.label: Why not figure out the content first?

mid: I wrote a mystery novel called 'The Culprit Is Among Us,' but everyone says the twist feels kind of underwhelming.

lines.text: Writing at Mocha's café actually helps me focus. Nice and quiet.

fallback_lines: Writing at Mocha's café used to be one of my life's little joys.
Feels a lot more boring now.

high: Sometimes I wonder what I'm even living for.

high.text: I guess it's just a pain you can't avoid, once you're born human.

high: A customer I'd never seen before bought three of my books today!
Sometimes I can't tell if never giving up is a talent or just stubbornness.

high.text: Still, this is the only thing I know how to do.

low: Another week gone. How many sentences did I even write this week...
The bookstore gets a few more customers on Fridays. Good thing.
Never wrote a single one of the chapters I was aiming for this week. Next week I'm really seeing it through.
mid: I don't really know how to give up. Not sure if that's a strength or a flaw.
I just keep writing, even if no one reads it.
I wrote a novel called 'The Detective's Last Footsteps,' but honestly I couldn't settle on an ending so I just wrapped it up.
I'll fix it later if I think of something.
On days when the writing won't come, I just tend to the flowering trees instead. It puts my mind at ease.
high: Talking with you gives me all kinds of story ideas. Thanks!
You've got so much experience, I feel like you hand me all sorts of stories.

high.text: Finally finished a whole chapter today! Had a little celebration for myself.

high: Everyone says my novels aren't interesting, but I don't let that get to me.
I'm going to keep writing anyway.

low: A few more people come to the bookstore on weekends.
Set up a new-releases corner on Saturday.
Did a new release come out, you ask?
Nope!
Writing at the café is my little pleasure on weekends.
mid: I love sitting at the café to write. The atmosphere just fits.
Want to come along next time?
I wrote a novel called 'The Letter I Never Sent' — honestly, I've got a few letters like that myself.

lines: Stopped by Flora's shop today to look at seeds. Didn't really need to buy anything.
fallback_lines: What should I do today?
Want to go somewhere nice together if you know a good spot?
...Never mind. Better go sell some books.

high: Someday, everyone's going to read my story. For real.
Poli bought my book today and then asked me to sign it!

high.text: First time anyone's ever asked me for that in my life.

high: Everyone calls me a dreamer with no sense, but it beats having no dream at all.
At least, that's what I think.

low: Opened the bookstore at a leisurely pace on Sunday.
Just like Newton made his great discovery under an apple tree, I'll probably write my masterpiece under a flowering tree someday.
Somehow the writing's just flowing today. Days like this are rare.
mid: Didn't sell many books today.
Though honestly, that's pretty much always the case...
Well, just because I haven't done well so far doesn't mean it's a real problem.
I also wrote a short story called 'He Who Always Stood in That Alley,' but not many people know about it.
I just rest at home on Sundays, tidying up my potted plants.
A regular break helps good inspiration come to me.
high: Want to try reading one of my novels sometime? ...Or maybe it's better if I don't show you yet.

high.text: Even I'm pretty happy with the short story I finished today!

high: Someday I want to write a truly great story.
I don't know when that'll be, but I'm sure it'll happen if I keep writing.

rain_conversation: Strangely, the writing flows well on rainy days.
When it rains, I don't have to water the pots. Makes things easy.
mail_reaction: '{player_mail_content}' — I could totally use this as a line in a novel. I'm being serious.

mail_reaction.text: Saw your mail. '{player_mail_content}' — that's so romantic. You know I love this stuff, right?

horror_conversation.text: {victim_name} keeps seeping into my novel. I don't even mean for it to happen.

horror_conversation: It's strange — even when I try not to, my hand just goes there.
The book {victim_name} bought is still sitting in the bookstore's stock.

horror_conversation.text: For some reason, I just can't bring myself to touch that shelf.

greeting.title: Prologue
lines: New work's prologue: 'One day, a stranger appeared in the unfamiliar town.'
Okay, it's really just a check-in letter. Starting with a prologue just sounds more impressive.
What have you been up to? I'm still wrestling with a single sentence.

greeting.title: Doing inventory
lines: I was counting stock of 'Beyond the Door' and thought of you.
I don't even know why. It just happened.
Come by the bookstore if you're bored. New releases... not yet.

greeting.title: Flowering-tree update
lines: The flowering tree finally sprouted new buds. Isn't that amazing?
Wasn't sure this was even worth writing about, but I wrote it anyway.
Anyway, you doing well?

event_invite.title: That bird-meat dish, I mean it
lines: That bird-meat dish yesterday was seriously delicious.
Story ideas kept popping into my head while I ate. But I forgot them all.
Invite me again. I'll try to remember next time.

event_invite.title: Thanks for the invite
lines: Thanks for inviting me yesterday.
Got to take a break from writing and just enjoy myself for once.
Turns out this kind of thing isn't bad every now and then.

alibi_reminder.title: Doing okay?
lines: Right in front of your house — that genuinely gave me chills. Are you all right?
{player_name}, come by the bookstore sometime to clear your head.

gift_thanks.title: Mind if I sneak this into my next novel?
lines: Thanks for the gift. Seriously, exactly my taste.
Mind if it makes a cameo in my next novel? I'll change the name, of course.
Well, nobody reads it anyway, so maybe it doesn't matter.

gift_thanks.title: Thank you
lines: I was so thrilled to get the gift.
Put it right on my desk. I'll glance at it whenever I get stuck writing.
Really, thank you.

memento_reminder.title: The story won't end without you
lines: My story keeps staying unfinished because you haven't come by.
There's something I want to give you. Would you come to the bookstore?

player_arrival_day_3.title: Come visit the bookstore
lines: Heard you just moved here! I'm Usher, this town's bookstore owner and novelist.
There's exactly one copy of my book left in stock — doesn't that feel like fate?
Come by if you're bored. Even just browsing is fine.
